body:
Full-codebase review, server finding 5 of 6. Reproduced.

`routes/sync.py` applies the push, then builds the delta, then commits. `delta` raises `403 not_a_member` when `full_lists` names a list the caller is not on — after the push has been applied and before the commit — so teardown rolls the push back. Measured: a brand-new list pushed in the same request as a stale `full_lists` entry is gone afterwards. The client retries the same request with the same `full_lists`, so the push is lost indefinitely rather than delayed. Android reaches this on its `syncNow(fullLists + listId)` retry path when that list is one the account has left.

The route already handles the analogous case correctly for a stale cursor: it commits before re-raising the 410.

Fix direction: validate `full_lists` membership before `apply_changes`, or commit the push before raising, as the cursor path does.
title: sync: a 403 from the delta discards the push already applied in the same request
